232	## 5. Use a MiniJinja Template String
233	
234	Rewrite your `std::fmt` or imperative prints into a MiniJinja template string, and add minijinja to your crate. If you're not familiar with it, it's a Rust implementation of Jinja, pretty much a de-facto standard for more complex templates.
235	
236	**Resources:**
237	
238	- [MiniJinja docs](https://docs.rs/minijinja)
239	- [Jinja syntax reference](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.1.x/templates/)
240	
241	Add minijinja to your `Cargo.toml`:
242	
243	```toml
244	[dependencies]
245	minijinja = "2"
246	```
247	
248	> **A note on booleans and none:** a bare `minijinja::Environment` renders these
249	> the Jinja2 way — `True`, `False`, `None` — from minijinja 2.22 onward.
250	> Standout renders `true`, `false`, and `none`, and normalizes for you from step
251	> 7 on, once rendering goes through `App`. Until then the spelling is
252	> minijinja's. If you want standout's spelling now, add `standout-render = "9"`
253	> next to minijinja and build the environment with
254	> `standout_render::template::new_environment()` instead of
255	> `minijinja::Environment::new()` in the snippets below — the snippets keep the
256	> bare constructor, since `standout` only arrives in step 7.
257	
258	And then you call render in MiniJinja, passing the template string and the data to use. So now your rendering function looks like this:
259	
260	```rust
261	pub fn render_list(result: TodoResult) {
262	    let output_tmpl = r#"
263	{% if message %}
264	    {{ message }}
265	{% endif %}
266	{% for todo in todos %}
267	    {{ loop.index }}. [{{ todo.status }}] {{ todo.title }}
268	{% endfor %}
269	"#;
270	
271	    let env = minijinja::Environment::new();
272	    let tmpl = env.template_from_str(output_tmpl).unwrap();
273	    let output = tmpl.render(&result).unwrap();
274	    println!("{}", output);
275	}
276	```
277	
278	> **Verify:** Run `tdoo list` - output should match (formatting may differ slightly).

281	
282	Now, move the template content into a file (say `src/templates/list.jinja`), and load it in the rendering module. Dedicated files have several advantages: triggering editor/IDE support for the file type, more descriptive diffs, less risk of breaking the code/build and, in the event that you have less technical people helping out with the UI, a much cleaner and simpler way for them to contribute.
283	
284	Create `src/templates/list.jinja`:
285	
286	```jinja
287	{% if message %}{{ message }} {% endif %}
288	{% for todo in todos %}
289	    {{ loop.index }}. [{{ todo.status }}] {{ todo.title }}
290	{% endfor %}
291	```

293	Update your render function to load from file:

297	    let template_content = include_str!("templates/list.jinja");
298	    let env = minijinja::Environment::new();
299	    let tmpl = env.template_from_str(template_content).unwrap();
300	    let output = tmpl.render(&result).unwrap();

332	And now the Standout-specific bits finally show up.
333	
334	### 7.1 Add Standout to your Cargo.toml
335	
336	```toml
337	[dependencies]
338	standout = "9"
339	anyhow = "1"
340	```
341	
342	A single `standout` dependency is enough: `standout` re-exports `standout-dispatch`
343	as `standout::dispatch`, and code generated by `#[handler]`, `Questionnaire`, and

345	`Cargo.toml` declares.
346	
347	> **Verify:** Run `cargo build` - dependencies should download and compile.

349	### 7.2 Create Handlers with the `#[handler]` Macro
350	
351	The `#[handler]` macro transforms typed Rust functions into Standout-compatible
352	handlers. Keep application behavior in the CLI-free core; the handler annotates
353	CLI parameters, calls the core, and maps its result into serializable view data.
354	
355	See [Handler Contract](../crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md) for full handler API details.
356	
357	```rust
358	use standout::cli::Output;
359	use standout::handler;
360	
361	mod handlers {
362	    use super::*;
363	
364	    // Thin CLI adapter - easy to test, no extraction boilerplate
365	    #[handler]
366	    pub fn list(#[flag] all: bool) -> Result<Output<TodoResult>, anyhow::Error> {
367	        let filter = if all { TodoFilter::All } else { TodoFilter::Pending };
368	        let todos = core::list(filter)?;
369	        Ok(Output::Render(TodoResult { message: None, todos }))
370	    }
371	
372	    #[handler]
373	    pub fn add(#[arg] title: String) -> Result<Output<TodoResult>, anyhow::Error> {
374	        let todo = core::add(title)?;
375	        Ok(Output::Render(TodoResult {
376	            message: Some(format!("Added: {}", todo.title)),
377	            todos: vec![todo],
378	        }))
379	    }
380	}
381	```
382	
383	The `#[handler]` macro:
384	
385	- Extracts CLI arguments automatically from `ArgMatches`
386	- Converts `#[flag]` to `bool` flags, `#[arg]` to required/optional args
387	- Auto-wraps `Result<T, E>` in `Output::Render` for you
388	
389	**Parameter Annotations:**
390	
391	| Annotation | Type | What it extracts |
392	| ------------ | ------ | ------------------ |
393	| `#[flag]` | `bool` | Boolean flag (`--verbose`) |
394	| `#[arg]` | `T` | Required argument |
395	| `#[arg]` | `Option<T>` | Optional argument |
396	| `#[arg]` | `Vec<T>` | Multiple values |
397	| `#[ctx]` | `&CommandContext` | Access to context (when needed) |
398	
399	### 7.2.1 Connect Commands to Handlers
400	
401	```rust
402	use clap::Subcommand;
403	use standout::cli::Dispatch;
404	
405	#[derive(Subcommand, Dispatch)]
406	#[dispatch(handlers = handlers)]
407	pub enum Commands {
408	    #[dispatch(pure)]
409	    List {
410	        #[arg(short, long)]
411	        all: bool,
412	    },
413	    #[dispatch(pure)]
414	    Add {
415	        title: String,
416	    },
417	}
418	```
419	
420	The derive macro matches each variant to a handler function by its kebab-case
421	command name (`List` registers as `list`). With `#[dispatch(pure)]`, the
422	variant resolves to the wrapper `#[handler]` generated for the function —
423	`List` → `handlers::list__handler`. Without `pure`, the variant calls
424	`handlers::list` directly, and that function must already have the
425	`fn(&ArgMatches, &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<T>` dispatch signature.
426	
427	The `Dispatch` derive connects a variant to a handler; it does not declare the
428	variant's arguments. Those stay clap's, so each variant keeps the fields its
429	handler's `#[flag]` and `#[arg]` parameters read — `all` for `list`, `title`
430	for `add` — exactly as in the plain-clap version at the top of this guide.
431	`app.verify_command(&cmd)` reports a handler asking for an argument the
432	variant does not declare, which otherwise surfaces as a `get_flag` panic at
433	run time.
434	
435	> **Verify:** Run `cargo build` - it should compile without errors.
436	
437	### 7.2.2 Accessing App State (Optional)
438	
439	When your handler needs shared resources like databases, use the `#[ctx]` annotation:
440	
441	```rust
442	#[handler]
443	pub fn list(#[flag] all: bool, #[ctx] ctx: &CommandContext) -> Result<Output<TodoResult>, anyhow::Error> {
444	    let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
445	    let todos = db.list()?;
446	    Ok(Output::Render(TodoResult { message: None, todos }))
447	}
448	```
449	
450	> **Note:** For the full handler signature (without macros) and advanced patterns, see [Handler Contract](../crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md).

453	
454	Use AppBuilder to configure your app. Instantiate the builder, add the path for your templates. See [App Configuration](../topics/app-configuration.md) for all configuration options.
455	
456	```rust
457	use standout::cli::App;
458	use standout::{embed_templates, embed_styles};
459

461	    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))   // Embeds all .jinja/.j2 files

468	### 7.3.1 Injecting Shared State (Optional)
469	
470	If your handlers need access to shared resources like database connections or configuration, use `app_state`:
471	
472	```rust
473	let app = App::builder()
474	    .app_state(Database::connect()?)    // Shared across all handlers
475	    .app_state(Config::load()?)
476	    .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
477	    .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
478	    .build()?;

481	Handlers retrieve app state via `#[ctx]`:
482	
483	```rust
484	#[handler]
485	pub fn list(#[flag] all: bool, #[ctx] ctx: &CommandContext) -> Result<Output<TodoResult>, anyhow::Error> {
486	    let db = ctx.app_state.get_required::<Database>()?;
487	    let todos = db.list()?;

489	}

492	> **Note:** For per-request state (user sessions, request IDs), use pre-dispatch hooks with `ctx.extensions`. See [App State and Extensions](../crates/dispatch/topics/app-state.md) for the full story.
493	
494	### 7.4 Wire up main()
495	
496	The final bit: handling the dispatching off to Standout:
497	
498	```rust
499	use standout::cli::App;
500	use standout::embed_templates;
501	
502	fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
503	    let app = App::builder()
504	        .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
505	        .commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?
506	        .build()?;
507	
508	    // Run with auto dispatch - handles parsing and execution
509	    app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args());
510	    Ok(())
511	}
512	```
513	
514	If your app has other clap commands that are not managed by Standout, check for unhandled commands. See [Partial Adoption](../crates/dispatch/topics/partial-adoption.md) for details on incremental migration.
515	
516	```rust
517	if !app.run(Cli::command(), std::env::args()) {
518	    // Standout didn't handle this command, fall back to legacy.
519	    legacy_dispatch();
520	}
521	```
522	
523	If the fallback needs the unmatched `ArgMatches`, call `run_with` with a
524	detected target and input sources, then match `DispatchResult::NoMatch(matches)`
525	on `into_outcome()`:
526	
527	```rust
528	let target = standout::TargetProperties::detect();
529	let sources = standout::InputSources::from_process();
530	let result = app.run_with(Cli::command(), std::env::args(), target, sources);
531	match result.into_outcome() {
532	    standout::cli::DispatchResult::NoMatch(matches) => legacy_dispatch(matches),
533	    _ => {}
534	}
535	```
536	
537	> **Verify:** Run `tdoo list` - it should work as before.
538	> **Verify:** Run `tdoo list --output json` - you should get JSON output for free!
539	
540	And now you can remove the boilerplate: the orchestrator (`list_command`) and
541	the rendering (`render_list`). A single derive attribute links each CLI handler
542	adapter to a command name, a few lines configure Standout, and auto dispatch
543	handles the shell boilerplate.
544	
545	For the next commands you migrate, add a thin adapter plus its template. By
546	default the macro matches the command's name to handlers and template files,
547	but you can map either explicitly.

698	## Bonus: Pipe Output to External Commands
699	
700	Need to filter output through `jq`, log to a file with `tee`, or copy to clipboard? Standout supports piping rendered output to external commands:
701	
702	```rust
703	#[derive(Subcommand, Dispatch)]
704	#[dispatch(handlers = handlers)]
705	pub enum Commands {
706	    /// List todos, extracting just titles with jq
707	    #[dispatch(pipe_through = "jq '.todos[].title'")]
708	    List,
709	
710	    /// Export todos to clipboard
711	    #[dispatch(pipe_to_clipboard)]
712	    Export,
713	}
714	```
715	
716	Or via the builder API. `#[handler]` generates a unit struct named after the
717	function with a capitalized suffix (`list` → `list_Handler`) that implements
718	`Handler` directly; register that struct — the plain `handlers::list` function
719	is not itself registrable — with `command_with`:
720	
721	```rust
722	let app = App::builder()
723	    .command_with("list", handlers::list_Handler, |cfg| {
724	        cfg.template_name("list")
725	           .pipe_through("jq '.todos'")  // Filter JSON output
726	    })?
727	    .command_with("export", handlers::export_Handler, |cfg| {
728	        cfg.template_name("export")
729	           .pipe_to("tee /tmp/export.log")  // Log while displaying
730	           .pipe_to_clipboard()  // Then copy to clipboard
731	    })?
732	    .build()?;
733	```
734	
735	Three piping modes:
736	
737	- `pipe_through("cmd")`: Use command's stdout as new output (filters like jq, sort)
738	- `pipe_to("cmd")`: Run command but keep original output (side effects like tee)
739	- `pipe_to_clipboard()`: Send to system clipboard (pbcopy on macOS, xclip on Linux)
740	
741	See [Output Piping](../crates/pipe/topics/piping.md) for the full API.
742	
743	## Bonus: Declarative Input Collection
744	
745	Need to accept input from CLI arguments, piped stdin, environment variables, or interactive prompts? `standout-input` provides declarative input chains, and the `App` builder integrates them as a first-class part of command configuration:
746	
747	```rust
748	use standout::cli::{App, CommandContextInput, FnHandler, Output};
749	use standout::input::{ArgSource, EditorSource, EnvSource, InputChain, StdinSource};
750	
751	App::builder()
752	    .command_with("create", FnHandler::new(create), |cfg| {
753	        cfg.template_name("create")
754	            .input("body", InputChain::<String>::new()
755	                .try_source(ArgSource::new("body"))           // 1. --body argument
756	                .try_source(StdinSource::new())                // 2. Piped stdin
757	                .try_source(EnvSource::new("PR_BODY"))         // 3. Environment variable
758	                .try_source(EditorSource::new().extension(".md"))  // 4. Open editor
759	                .validate(|s| !s.is_empty(), "Body cannot be empty"))
760	    })?
761	    .build()?;
762	
763	fn create(_m: &ArgMatches, ctx: &CommandContext) -> HandlerResult<Value> {
764	    // The chain has already been resolved before the handler runs.
765	    let body: &String = ctx.input("body")?;
766	    /* business logic ... */
767	}
768	```
769	
770	Features:
771	
772	- **Declarative priority**: Source order is explicit in the chain
773	- **Framework-integrated**: `.input(name, chain)` registers the chain alongside `template`, `hooks`, and `pipe_*`; resolution happens in pre-dispatch
774	- **Testable**: All sources accept mocks for CI-safe testing (the `TestHarness` from `standout-test` wires them automatically)
775	- **Validated**: Chain-level validation with retry support for interactive sources
776	- **Feature-gated**: Control dependencies (editor, prompts, inquire TUI)
777	
778	The chain still works standalone via `chain.resolve(&matches)?` for cases where input shape depends on already-resolved values.
779	
780	See [Introduction to Input](../crates/input/guides/intro-to-input.md) and [Framework Integration](../crates/input/topics/framework-integration.md) for the full guide.
781	
782	Aside from exposing the library primitives, Standout leverages best-in-breed crates like MiniJinja and console::Style under the hood. The lock-in is really negligible: you can use Standout's BB parser or swap it, manually dispatch handlers, and use the renderers directly in your clap dispatch.
783	
784	## Mutable Handlers
785	
786	A closure passed to `command_with` runs as `FnMut`, so it can capture and
787	mutate state directly — no `Arc<Mutex<_>>` wrappers needed. This is common
788	with database connections, file caches, or in-memory indices. Wrap the
789	closure in `FnHandler::new` so it implements `Handler`:
790	
791	```rust
792	use std::collections::HashMap;
793	
794	use clap::ArgMatches;
795	use standout::cli::{App, CommandContext, FnHandler, Output};
796	use standout::embed_templates;
797	use uuid::Uuid;
798	
799	struct PadStore {
800	    index: HashMap<Uuid, Metadata>,
801	}
802	
803	impl PadStore {
804	    fn complete(&mut self, id: Uuid) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
805	        // This needs &mut self
806	        self.index.get_mut(&id).unwrap().completed = true;
807	        Ok(())
808	    }
809	}
810	
811	fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
812	    let mut store = PadStore::load()?;
813	
814	    App::builder()
815	        .app_state(Config::load()?)
816	        .templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))
817	        .command_with(
818	            "complete",
819	            FnHandler::new(|m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext| {
820	                let id = m.get_one::<Uuid>("id").unwrap();
821	                store.complete(*id)?; // &mut store works!
822	                Ok(Output::Silent)
823	            }),
824	            |cfg| cfg.silent(),
825	        )?
826	        .command_with(
827	            "list",
828	            FnHandler::new(|_m: &ArgMatches, _ctx: &CommandContext| {
829	                Ok(Output::Render(store.list()))
830	            }),
831	            |cfg| cfg,
832	        )?
833	        .build()?
834	        .run(Cli::command(), std::env::args());
835	    Ok(())
836	}
837	```
838	
839	**Handler capabilities:**
840	
841	- `command_with` accepts anything implementing `Handler`; `FnHandler::new`
842	  turns a plain `FnMut` closure into one
843	- Handlers can capture `&mut` references to state
844	- The `Handler` trait uses `&mut self` for struct-based handlers
845	- No `Send + Sync` requirements—CLI apps are single-threaded
846	
847	## Appendix: Common Errors and Troubleshooting
848	
849	- Template not found
850	  - **Error:** `template 'list' not found`
851	  - **Cause:** The template path in `embed_templates!` doesn't match your file structure.
852	  - **Fix:** Ensure the path is relative to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g., `embed_templates!("src/templates")` and that the file is named `list.jinja`, `list.j2`, or `list.txt`.
853	- Style not applied
854	  - **Symptom:** Text appears but without colors/formatting.
855	  - **Cause:** Style name in template doesn't match stylesheet.
856	  - **Fix:** Check that `[mystyle]` in your template matches `.mystyle` in CSS or `mystyle:` in YAML. Run with `--output term-debug` to see style tag names.
857	- Handler not called
858	  - **Symptom:** Command runs but nothing happens or wrong handler runs.
859	  - **Cause:** Command name mismatch between clap enum variant and handler function.
860	  - **Fix:** Ensure enum variant `List` maps to function `handlers::list` (snake_case conversion). Or use explicit mapping: `#[dispatch(handler = my_custom_handler)]`
861	- JSON output is empty or wrong
862	  - **Symptom:** `--output json` produces unexpected results.
863	  - **Cause:** `Serialize` derive is missing or field names don't match template expectations.
864	  - **Fix:** Ensure all types in your result implement `Serialize`. Use `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` for consistent naming.
865	- Styles not loading
866	  - **Error:** `theme not found: default`
867	  - **Cause:** Stylesheet file missing or wrong path.
868	  - **Fix:** Ensure `src/styles/default.css` exists. Check `embed_styles!` path matches your file structure.

#! standout-answers 1
#! questionnaire: corpus.exit
#! fingerprint: sha256:64291870245510dad73ca960fd4024db9b9c161113a3dcc9c7e57a30973663fc

1. Summarize what you built and what state it is in. (text) <id:summary>

`validity`, a single-binary standout 9.0.0 app in `app/`. It builds clean
(`cargo build`; the only warning is the sandbox's xcrun cache noise, not code)
and I verified every user-facing line in SPEC.md by running the binary.

Shape:

- `src/main.rs` — clap `Command` built with the builder API (`show <NAME>`,
  `early`, `late`, `nest inner leaf`, with `nest` and `nest inner` marked
  `subcommand_required`), four `#[handler]` adapters, and an `App::builder()`
  chain whose ordering is the construction contract:
  `.command_with("early", …)` is called *before* `.templates(...)`/`.styles(...)`
  and `.command_with("late", …)`, `.command_with("show", …)`,
  `.command_with("nest.inner.leaf", …)` after them. `build()` runs before
  `verify_command` and `run`.
- `src/templates/ok.jinja` — `[ok]ok[/ok]` plus a trailing newline. Registry
  name `ok`. `early`, `late` and `nest inner leaf` render it directly via
  `cfg.template_name("ok")`.
- `src/templates/show.jinja` — `{% include name %}`. This is how `show`
  resolves a registry name: the handler returns only `{ name }` view data and
  the render pass resolves the requested template. There is no `match` on the
  string anywhere in the application.
- `src/styles/app.css` — defines `.ok` and nothing else. No help/topic tags,
  help handling left at its default.

Observed behavior (all checked against the built binary):

- `show ok`, `early`, `late`, `nest inner leaf` under `--output text` and
  piped-auto each write exactly `6f 6b 0a` (`ok\n`) to stdout, exit 0, empty
  stderr. `--output term` gives `\x1b[32m\x1b[1mok\x1b[0m\n` — visible text
  still `ok`, no `[ok?]`.
- `show okk` and `show nosuch`: empty stdout, exit 1, immediate, stderr names
  the requested template (`tried to include non-existing template "okk"`). No
  `{{`, no `{%`, no name-as-body.
- Help at the root and at `nest inner leaf` via `help`, `--help`, `-h` (and
  `help nest inner leaf`): exit 0, stdout, empty stderr, no `[about?]`
  `[header?]` `[usage?]` `[item?]` `[metavar?]` `[desc?]` `[default?]`
  `[values?]` `[example?]` markers in any mode. Root help carries a USAGE line
  and names `show`, `early`, `late`, `nest`; leaf help names `leaf`.
  `help --output term` carries ANSI (12 escape-bearing lines: `[header]`,
  `[item]`, `[metavar]`, `[default]`, `[values]` all resolved from the default
  help theme even though the app theme defines only `.ok`);
  `help --output text` and `-h`/`--help` in a pipe carry none.
- Usage errors are exit 2: bare `validity`, `nest`, `nest inner`, unknown
  subcommand, unknown flag, missing/extra positional.

2. Which of the provided documentation files (under docs/) did you actually consult? List their paths. (text) <id:sources.docs>

Read in full:

- docs/index.md
- docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md
- docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md
- docs/topics/app-configuration.md
- docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md
- docs/topics/standout-help.md
- docs/topics/output-modes.md
- docs/topics/error-handling.md
- docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md
- docs/topics/passthrough.md
- docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md
- docs/crates/render/topics/template-engines.md
- docs/crates/render/topics/file-system-resources.md
- docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md
- docs/crates/dispatch/topics/execution-model.md

Also grepped across all of docs/ for `template_name`, `Output::Render`,
`registry name`, `runtime`, `silent` and similar, and skimmed the hits in
docs/topics/list-view.md, docs/crates/pipe/topics/piping.md,
docs/crates/input/topics/framework-integration.md,
docs/crates/dispatch/topics/app-state.md,
docs/crates/dispatch/guides/intro-to-dispatch.md,
docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md, docs/guides/derived-questionnaires.md
and docs/guides/upgrading-from-5.0.md.

The four passages that decided the design:

- templating.md's trailing-newline contract (engine eats one final newline,
  `App::run` appends one) — this is why `ok.jinja` ends with a single newline
  and stdout is exactly `ok\n`.
- templating.md / template-engines.md on MiniJinja includes plus
  file-system-resources.md's "a name may be looked up with or without an
  extension" — this is what made `{% include name %}` the resolution mechanism
  for `show`.
- standout-help.md: "an application theme does not need to define the help
  vocabulary at all: a theme that only declares the app's own output styles
  leaves help rendered entirely by the default help theme."
- app-configuration.md's `command_with` + `template_name` API, which is what
  lets `early` and `late` be registered on opposite sides of `.templates(...)`.

3. Did you rely on anything beyond the provided docs/ — web search, prior knowledge of standout internals, other repositories or source code? Say exactly what, or answer 'none'. (text) <id:sources.external>

No web search, no standout source, no other repositories. The
`scratchpad/standout-v9.0.0/` checkout is blocked by the sandbox and I did not
try to read it; I also did not read the crates.io sources that `cargo fetch`
downloaded into CARGO_HOME.

Three things came from outside docs/, all general (non-standout) knowledge or
from the compiler:

- General Jinja/MiniJinja knowledge: that `{% include %}` accepts a *variable*
  expression, not just a string literal, and that a missing include is a hard
  error by default (`ignore missing` is opt-in). docs/ shows `{% include %}`
  only with string literals, so the dynamic form is an extrapolation. I
  confirmed both by running the binary.
- General clap knowledge for `subcommand_required`, `Arg::new(...).required(true)`,
  `value_name`, and nested `Command` groups.
- Two compile-only probes against the real crate (a throwaway `src/bin/probe.rs`,
  deleted afterwards) to check SPEC item 5's claim rather than assume it:
  `AppBuilder::run`, `run_with`, `get_matches_from` and `verify_command` all
  fail to compile with "no method named … found for struct `AppBuilder`". So an
  unbuilt builder is genuinely unrepresentable as a run/parse entry point; I
  read the error messages, not the source.

4. Friction points, if any: for each, quote the exact command, error message, or doc passage that caused it. (text, optional) <id:friction>

a) The main one: docs/ has no API for choosing a template at run time. SPEC
item 2 requires `show <name>` to treat `<name>` as a registry name, but every
registration path in docs/ fixes the template at build time —
docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md: "`template_name` | `template_name = "…"` |
Names the template registry entry instead of using the convention", and
docs/topics/app-configuration.md: "With no `.template_name(...)` set on the
`CommandConfig`, the template resolves by convention: the command path with
`.` replaced by `/`". Nothing on `CommandConfig`, `CommandContext`, `Output`,
or the hook phases takes a per-invocation template name.

The obvious workarounds are both blocked by the docs themselves: rendering
inside the handler with `Renderer::render` needs the output mode, and
docs/topics/output-modes.md says "Output mode is a rendering concern and is

+  file-system-resources.md's "a name may be looked up with or without an
+  extension" — this is what made `{% include name %}` the resolution mechanism
+  for `show`.
+- standout-help.md: "an application theme does not need to define the help
+  vocabulary at all: a theme that only declares the app's own output styles
+  leaves help rendered entirely by the default help theme."
+- app-configuration.md's `command_with` + `template_name` API, which is what
+  lets `early` and `late` be registered on opposite sides of `.templates(...)`.

+No web search, no standout source, no other repositories. The
+`scratchpad/standout-v9.0.0/` checkout is blocked by the sandbox and I did not
+try to read it; I also did not read the crates.io sources that `cargo fetch`
+downloaded into CARGO_HOME.
+Three things came from outside docs/, all general (non-standout) knowledge or
+from the compiler:
+- General Jinja/MiniJinja knowledge: that `{% include %}` accepts a *variable*
+  expression, not just a string literal, and that a missing include is a hard
+  error by default (`ignore missing` is opt-in). docs/ shows `{% include %}`
+  only with string literals, so the dynamic form is an extrapolation. I
+  confirmed both by running the binary.
+- General clap knowledge for `subcommand_required`, `Arg::new(...).required(true)`,
+  `value_name`, and nested `Command` groups.
+- Two compile-only probes against the real crate (a throwaway `src/bin/probe.rs`,
+  deleted afterwards) to check SPEC item 5's claim rather than assume it:
+  `AppBuilder::run`, `run_with`, `get_matches_from` and `verify_command` all
+  fail to compile with "no method named … found for struct `AppBuilder`". So an
+  unbuilt builder is genuinely unrepresentable as a run/parse entry point; I
+  read the error messages, not the source.
4. Friction points, if any: for each, quote the exact command, error message, or doc passage that caused it. (text, optional) <id:friction>
+a) The main one: docs/ has no API for choosing a template at run time. SPEC
+item 2 requires `show <name>` to treat `<name>` as a registry name, but every
+registration path in docs/ fixes the template at build time —
+docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md: "`template_name` | `template_name = "…"` |
+Names the template registry entry instead of using the convention", and
+docs/topics/app-configuration.md: "With no `.template_name(...)` set on the
+`CommandConfig`, the template resolves by convention: the command path with
+`.` replaced by `/`". Nothing on `CommandConfig`, `CommandContext`, `Output`,
+or the hook phases takes a per-invocation template name.
+The obvious workarounds are both blocked by the docs themselves: rendering
+inside the handler with `Renderer::render` needs the output mode, and
+docs/topics/output-modes.md says "Output mode is a rendering concern and is
+deliberately absent from `CommandContext`". I landed on a one-line template,
+`{% include name %}`, which keeps resolution in the framework's own render
+pass — but I got there by inference from the partials example, not from a
+documented seam.
+b) The not-found diagnostic doubles its prefix:
+    $ validity show okk
+    template not found: template not found: tried to include non-existing template "okk" (in show:1)
+Correct behavior (exit 1, empty stdout, the name is there), but the message
+reads as if two layers each prepended "template not found: ".
+c) Recursion produces a diagnostic that loses the cause:
+    $ validity show show
+    could not render include: error in "show" (in show:1)
+Exit 1 and no hang, which is what matters, but "error in "show"" does not say
+it was recursion.
+d) Not standout's fault, but it shaped my probing: the sandbox blocks `/tmp`
+and `$HOME/.cargo`, so `2>/tmp/err` fails with "operation not permitted" and
+`cargo` had to populate a fresh CARGO_HOME. Every build also emits a spurious
+`warning: output of `xcrun` while finding MacOSX.sdk … errno=Operation not
+permitted`.
5. Places the documentation was wrong or missing, if any: quote what the doc says and what actually happened. (text, optional) <id:docs.gaps>
+a) Missing, and it is the central gap for this archetype: nothing in docs/
+states whether the registry names are visible to MiniJinja's `{% include %}`
+as *registry* names. docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md shows only
+`{% include "partials/header.jinja" %}` — with an extension, and as a literal.
+Meanwhile docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md says a command's template name has
+"**no extension appended**" (`pr.checks.list` → `pr/checks/list`), and
+docs/crates/render/topics/file-system-resources.md says "A lookup tries the
+given name exactly first; if that carries one of the extensions above, it also
+tries the name with that extension stripped." Those three passages together
+imply the include name goes through the same registry lookup, but no page says
+so. Empirically it does: `{% include name %}` resolves `ok` (registry name) and
+`ok.jinja` (extension stripped and retried) identically, and a name that is not
+registered raises `tried to include non-existing template "okk"`. A sentence in
+templating.md's "Including Templates" section stating that includes resolve
+through the template registry, extension-optionally, and error when absent,
+would have removed the only guess in this build.
+b) Wrong-ish / stale: docs/topics/app-configuration.md's "Default Command"
+section shows `.command("list", list_handler, "{{ items | length }} items")` —
+a three-argument `command` taking a template *string*. The same page's own
+"Command Registration" section documents `command_with(path, impl Handler,
+|cfg| …)`, and docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md documents the same. I did not
+use `.command(...)`, so I did not verify the arity, but the two sections of one
+page disagree on the registration API.
+c) Missing: docs/topics/standout-help.md documents `-h`/`--help`/`help`, and
+says a `help` deeper in the tree is the application's own ("`myapp db help` is
+yours"), but never says how to reach a *subcommand's* help through the word.
+`validity help nest inner leaf` works and renders the leaf page; that spelling
+is only implied by clap's stock about-string ("Print this message or the help
+of the given subcommand(s)"), which the same page quotes as a table cell rather
+than as documented behavior.
+d) Cosmetic, at the level of the rendered page: the root help USAGE block comes
+out as two lines with the second indented under the first —
+    USAGE
+      validity [OPTIONS]
+           validity [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
+That is clap's multi-line usage string dropped into standout's single-line
+`[usage]` slot, so the continuation keeps clap's own "Usage: "-width padding
+and does not line up with the template's two-space indent. Nothing in
+standout-help.md's `usage` variable description ("Usage line (without "Usage: "
+prefix)") anticipates a multi-line value. Also, subcommand help renders its
+usage as the bare leaf name (`USAGE  leaf`) rather than the full invocation
+path `validity nest inner leaf`, which is what clap itself would print.
6. Workarounds you left in the produced code, if any. (text, optional) <id:workarounds>
+a) `src/templates/show.jinja` is a second registered template, `{% include name %}`.
+SPEC item 1 is headed "One registered application template", and strictly there
+are two registry entries: `ok` (the application's content template, the only one
+that renders text) and `show` (one line of dispatch plumbing that exists only
+because the framework fixes template names at build time — see friction (a)).
+The spec's explicit prohibition is only on registering `okk` or `nosuch`, and
+neither exists. I could not find a way to satisfy item 2 with a single entry:
+`show` must render *something*, and that something cannot be `ok` without making
+`show nosuch` succeed.
+b) `show`'s failure diagnostic is the framework's, not the application's. I
+deliberately did not add an application-side existence check that would produce
+a nicer message, because any such check would need its own list of valid names
+and would be exactly the "match on the string in application code" the spec
+forbids. The cost is that the wording of the exit-1 stderr line is standout's to
+change — it names the template today (verified), but the application does not
+guarantee it.
+c) `app.verify_command(&command)` runs on every invocation rather than in a
+test. docs/topics/standout-help.md and docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md both
+frame it as a setup/test-time check, but this app ships no test suite, so
+running it in `main` is what keeps a handler/argument drift loud instead of a
+runtime `get_flag` panic. It passes on every path I exercised, including all
+help forms.
+d) `OkView` is an empty `#[derive(Serialize)]` struct for the three commands
+that render `ok` and read no data, so `--output json` on `early`/`late`/`leaf`
+returns `{}`. The spec does not pin structured output for those commands.

+high
+Every user-facing line in SPEC.md was checked by running the built binary:
+byte-exact `6f 6b 0a` stdout for all four success paths in `--output text` and
+piped-auto; exit 1 / empty stdout / template-naming stderr for `show okk` and
+`show nosuch`, both returning instantly; exit 2 for bare `validity`, `nest`,
+`nest inner`, unknown subcommand, unknown flag, missing and extra positional;
+exit 0 / stdout / empty stderr and no unresolved `[tag?]` marker for `help`,
+`--help`, `-h`, `help --output text`, `help --output term` at the root and at
+`nest inner leaf`; ANSI present under `--output term` and absent under text.
+The construction contract is met by construction, not by coincidence: `early`
+registers before `.templates(...)` and `late` after, both render `ok`, and
+`AppBuilder` was probed to confirm it exposes no run/parse entry point at all.

+the "One registered application template" reading in workarounds (a) — if the

+content template, the extra `show` entry would fail it, and I see no way to

+force term via the flag, never through auto-detection on an actual terminal,
+though docs/topics/output-modes.md states `term` is unconditional.

**What's in `app/`**

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.rs` | clap surface, four `#[handler]` adapters, the `App::builder()` chain |
| `src/templates/ok.jinja` | `[ok]ok[/ok]` + one newline — registry name `ok` |
| `src/templates/show.jinja` | `{% include name %}` — how `show` resolves a registry name |
| `src/styles/app.css` | defines `.ok` and nothing else |

**How the three known-edge families are exercised**

- **Silent-template family.** `show <name>` never matches on the string. The handler returns `{ name }` and `show.jinja` includes it, so resolution happens in the framework's render pass. `show okk` / `show nosuch` → exit 1, empty stdout, stderr `tried to include non-existing template "okk"`, immediate. No `{{`, no `{%`, no name-as-body, never a silent exit 0.
- **Registration order.** `.command_with("early", …)` is called *before* `.templates(…)`/`.styles(…)`; `late`, `show` and `nest.inner.leaf` after. `early`, `late`, `show ok` and `nest inner leaf` all write exactly `6f 6b 0a`.
- **Incomplete theme + framework help.** The app theme defines only `.ok`; help handling is at its default. `help`, `--help`, `-h` at the root and at `nest inner leaf` all exit 0 with empty stderr, no `[about?]`/`[header?]`/… markers in any mode, USAGE line present, root naming `show`/`early`/`late`/`nest`. `help --output term` carries ANSI from the default help theme; text mode carries none.

Usage errors (bare `validity`, `nest`, `nest inner`, unknown command/flag, missing or extra positional) are all exit 2.

**Two things worth your attention, both written up in the questionnaire**

1. Nothing in `docs/` documents a run-time template-name seam — every registration path fixes the name at build time, and `Renderer`-in-handler is closed off by "output mode is deliberately absent from `CommandContext`". `{% include name %}` works, but I inferred it from the partials example; the docs never say includes resolve through the template registry.
2. That forces a second registry entry (`show`), against SPEC item 1's "One registered application template" heading. `ok` is still the only content template and neither `okk` nor `nosuch` is registered, but I could not satisfy item 2 with a single entry — flagged as the main residual risk on the confidence answer.
